args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all three regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why it went to production even though v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, and it was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, what we rolled back to, and that the service is healthy now.

One thing to look into: the test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was already failing in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I listed it in the incident as a follow-up, along with finding out why v2.3.1 failed.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
